verdict.summary: Blueprint v3 substantively honors synthesis claims, the rationale brief, the inherited ADRs, and the Gate-4 user-override decisions. The three Gate-4 user decisions (OI-1 drop-fallback, OI-2 Path A graduation, OI-3 hard gate) are all (a) reflected verbatim in the Blueprint's Open Items closure block, (b) codified in ADRs (ADR-0042, ADR-0043) and an ADR edit (ADR-0037 line 143 revert), and (c) load-bearing rationale preserved (especially OI-3's 'MCPs can cause a lot of problems' verbatim in ADR-0043). The 7-server inventory, 8-of-36 consumer set, 5-agent Serena allowlist, 36-agent demand-side sweep, C-0445 zero-mcp__ invariant, ADR-0040 design-iac/design-api hedge resolution, and ADR-0038 schema v1.1.0 blast-radius schema honoring are all CoVe-verified against synthesis + codebase-analysis + actual codebase state. Two important issues surfaced: (I-AA-001) the filename `.claude/agents/design-cc.md` is used in 3 locations (blueprint line 450, ADR-0040 line 137, propagated downstream into plan-v1.md and tasks.json) but the actual file in the repo is `design-claude-code.md` (the `design-cc` token is a frontmatter `name:` only, per the Path-A reserved-word workaround); without correction, plan execution would not find the file. (I-AA-002) The consumer-set math description is inconsistent across artifacts: blueprint line 830 says '7-agent base consumer-mapping' but cc-design's table has 6 concrete rows + 1 TBD that ADR-0040 fills, and the agent-roster-impact-matrix line 57 cites '7+5=12 minus 4 overlaps = 8' (the overlap count is actually 3, not 4). The final 8-unique-agent figure is correct and consistent, but the math narrative confuses future readers. No BLOCKER issues. Three MINOR/NIT clarity items also surfaced. Recommend a focused in-place amendment dispatch (blueprint-v3.0.1 patch-level revision) to correct the filename references (I-AA-001) and clarify the consumer-set math narrative (I-AA-002); the recommended fix is small and does not require a full Gate-4 re-author.

issues.description: Three artifacts describe the union math from three slightly-different angles, producing an internally inconsistent narrative even though the final 8-unique-agent figure is correct. (a) Blueprint line 830 says 'three of those five overlap with the 7-agent base consumer-mapping (review-architecture-auditor, design-cicd, discovery-codebase-researcher)' — but cc-design's consumer-mapping table has 6 concrete rows + 1 TBD that ADR-0040 fills, not '7 agents' (the 7th row was a placeholder, not an agent). (b) Blueprint line 399 (Fact Disposition C-0445 rationale) says '3 from base consumer-mapping ... overlap with the 5-agent ADR-0040 Serena allowlist; the other 5 are non-overlapping' — the 'other 5' phrasing is correct (5 = 8 total − 3 overlaps) but confusing because there isn't an obvious 5-agent grouping that's 'non-overlapping' (the 5 are actually 3 base-only + 2 Serena-only). (c) agent-roster-impact-matrix line 57 says '7+5=12 minus 4 overlaps = 8' — but the actual overlap count is 3, not 4 (review-architecture-auditor + design-cicd + discovery-codebase-researcher). The matrix's '7+5=12' uses the 7-rows-from-cc-design count which includes the TBD row that ADR-0040 fills; if the TBD row is consumed by ADR-0040's narrowing, it's not legitimate to count it twice. Correct math: 6 concrete base + 5 Serena − 3 overlap = 8 unique.
verification_chain: Read cc-design.md:200-216 → 7-row table where row 7 is 'TBD per D-13 narrowing'; only rows 1-6 list concrete agents (design-api, design-cicd, design-iac, discovery-external-researcher, discovery-codebase-researcher, review-architecture-auditor)
Read ADR-0040:62 → 5-agent Serena allowlist: review-architecture-auditor, design-cc, design-cicd, design-codespaces, discovery-codebase-researcher
Compute overlap: review-architecture-auditor (cc-design row 6 ∩ Serena), design-cicd (cc-design row 2 ∩ Serena), discovery-codebase-researcher (cc-design row 5 ∩ Serena) → 3 overlap items
Union: 6 concrete base + 5 Serena − 3 overlap = 8 unique. Final 8 figure is correct; the narrative '7-agent base' and 'minus 4 overlaps' are arithmetically inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'the 7-agent base consumer-mapping' (blueprint-v3.md:830) with 'the 6-agent base consumer-mapping (cc-design.md rows 1-6 — row 7 was the TBD that ADR-0040 narrowing filled)'. Replace agent-roster-impact-matrix.md:57 math '7+5=12, not 7+5=12' chain with the cleaner '6 concrete base rows + 5 ADR-0040 Serena consumers − 3 overlap = 8 unique union; cc-design.md row 7 was a TBD placeholder consumed by ADR-0040 narrowing, not double-counted'. Blueprint line 399's 'other 5 are non-overlapping' can stay or be clarified to 'the remaining 5 are net-new from the union perspective: 3 base-only (design-api, design-iac, discovery-external-researcher) + 2 Serena-only (design-claude-code/design-cc, design-codespaces)'. This is a clarity fix; the architectural decision and the 8-unique-agent final figure are unchanged. Bundle with I-AA-001 in the same patch-level dispatch.

issues.description: The orchestrator Gate-6 phase-validator wiring (Component 9, NEW v3 per ADR-0043) is listed as a Change Impact Map item (line 458) and as Component 9 (line 674). But the existing `execute-orchestrator.md` agent file is not listed among the touched agents in §Sub-Agents (8 of 36) — even though Gate-6 phase-validator behavior is invoked from orchestrator code. The Blueprint resolves this implicitly via 'phase-validator script update by plan-author' (Interface Change Matrix line 495); but the demand-side sweep at agent-roster-impact-matrix.md classified execute-orchestrator as EXPLICIT_NO. The asymmetry is real: the orchestrator's Gate-6 invocation logic must change to honor the hard gate, but the orchestrator agent file's `tools:` allowlist does not need to change (the orchestrator invokes auditing-mcp via Bash, not via mcp__ tool). The matrix's EXPLICIT_NO classification is correct for the consumer-set scope; the Blueprint's Component 9 + Interface Change Matrix is correct for the orchestrator's gate-logic change. But a reader could miss the layering. No factual error — completeness recommendation only.

issues.description: Per-Layer Test Strategy row for 'family-graduation structural test (NEW v3)' says 'manual at Gate 6 or in audit-skill OP-7 trifecta-consistency rule' — but OP-7 is the trifecta-consistency rule (KB-mcp-platform ↔ KB-mcp-design ↔ auditing-mcp). The family-graduation structural test (auditing-mcp frontmatter family: + Sub-skill family body section + auditing-cc-configs family-list pruning + auditing-shared cross-ref expansion) is not strictly trifecta-consistency; it's family-membership-consistency. Mapping it to OP-7 conflates two rule semantics. ADR-0042 Implementation Guidance does mention 'auditing-mcp augmentation gains family-graduation steps' (Implementation Plan step 8) but does not explicitly assign the graduation-structural-check to OP-7. Either (a) OP-7 should be explicitly broadened to include family-membership-consistency, with that documented in cc-design and/or ADR-0042, OR (b) the family-graduation structural test should be its own audit rule (e.g., OP-11 or a Sub-skill family-coordinator rule). Currently the Blueprint maps it ambiguously.

blueprint-v3.md:222 + cc-design.md:483 — OP-7 = 'trifecta consistency' rule semantics

issues.suggestion: Non-blocking. Either (a) tighten the OP-7 definition in cc-design / KB-mcp-design / ADR-0042 to explicitly include family-membership-consistency under the rule, OR (b) defer to plan-author to decide rule placement. Recommend (a) for clean semantic separation. Bundle with the patch-level dispatch if I-AA-001/002 trigger one.
